answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a slashing bond in its kernel registry before it can attest work. New identities start with a tiny trust delta, so creating many fake accounts yields little influence until each has completed verified jobs over time. Like layers of shale, reputation accretes slowly and cannot be copied: an attacker who misbehaves loses the bond and the accumulated history, so each additional identity costs real capital plus the time to earn trust, while honest agents keep their standing.
